items.note: Between-subjects experiment with 45 design students comparing self-reflection, written stepwise guidance, and an antagonistic AI agent while revising design proposals; outcomes are self-rated reconsideration plus counts of ideas generated/discarded and design improvements, with no rated creativity in the abstract, and n is below 50.

Two-section quasi-experiment in an undergraduate illustration studio (Midjourney ideation workflow n=82 vs conventional workflow n=80) with expert rubric scores for originality, appropriateness, and elaboration of final artefacts; assignment is by class section, not random.

System paper on a GAN-based sketch-to-image co-creation tool evaluated with 60 art students, reporting 35.4 percent higher expert-judged creative output quality than traditional tools; the comparison design is unclear (search notes say the full text may be a survey plus expert review), and the tool is a GAN rather than an LLM or diffusion model.

AEA RCT registry entry (no linked paper found): participants individually randomized to ChatGPT-assisted or independent business idea generation, then all generate and evaluate ideas without AI (after_ai); outcomes include idea quality; 200 is the planned sample, not an analyzed count.

Undergraduate research-journal study: 33 students randomly assigned to brainstorm with ChatGPT or alone before writing a poem; poems ranked for creativity and coded for strategies and unique words; n is below 50.

Experimental study comparing users of the scaffolded Supermind Ideator, plain ChatGPT users, and people working alone on idea innovativeness; N and assignment not stated; ACM CI 2024 conference version (10.1145/3643562.3672611) and an erratum exist, and arXiv 2311.01937 is an earlier system description.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar elided, Crossref, Springer page blocked); per search notes, two experiments vary the emotional valence and arousal of AI-generated inspirational images given to design learners and rate design creativity, an AI-variant (ai_design) comparison with no no-AI arm.

ISR paper with controlled lab experiments on students and real-world tests with professional designers comparing design work with and without GenAI at the ideation and execution stages; creativity of the work is the outcome; N and assignment are not in the abstract.

226 students in problem-based learning with GenAI assigned to a critical-thinking intervention (including AI-supported peer mentoring) or no intervention; both arms use GenAI, so the contrast is an instructional variant of AI use rather than an AI configuration, and originality and idea density are scored on group reports (unit may be the group).

Two-class quasi-experiment with 46 university students in digital game development: generative-AI co-regulated learning versus conventional co-regulated learning; reports project design performance and creative thinking (likely a scale), and n is below 50.
